metaDescription: Six battery sprayers for liquid fertilizer and lawn feed, compared on agitation, filtration, nozzle choice and tank size so salts do not clog or settle out.
expertTake: The Scotts 2 Gallon is the pick for most lawns because it pairs an in line filter and Viton seals with a lock on shut off, which is what liquid feed punishes. The Budstr 2 Gallon is the value pick, with a wide mouth tank and a stack of spare gaskets. Skip a battery unit entirely if you only feed a few pots, because a hose end feeder does that with no pump to clean.
introParagraphs: Liquid fertilizer is gentler on a sprayer than herbicide, but it has its own way of causing trouble. Dissolved salts crystallize in nozzles, undissolved particles clog filters, and a mix that sits unstirred settles out so the last tank is stronger or weaker than the first.

A good feeding sprayer therefore needs three things: a fine filter before the pump, a nozzle that gives an even band instead of a jet, and either agitation or a habit of shaking the tank. Battery power helps by keeping flow steady across a whole lawn pass.

products.description:
A fertilizer sprayer lives or dies by its filtration, and this is the one here with the clearest answer: an in line filter at the shut off that you can pull and rinse in seconds. Because liquid feed carries fine particles and salts, that screen is what keeps the nozzle from sputtering halfway across the lawn. Viton seals in the shut off add margin if the same sprayer later sees a weed product.

The lock on feature holds the valve open for broadcast passes, and the quoted capacity of up to twelve full tanks per charge means the battery will not be the limit on a typical yard. The 21 inch poly wand lets you keep the nozzle at a steady height, which matters for even coverage. Compared with the SideKing 2 Gallon it is sturdier at the valve end, and compared with the Petra HD2000-S it has a lighter, simpler body.

After feeding, run clear water through the wand until it comes out clean, because dried fertilizer in the in line screen is the most common cause of a weak spray next season. Store it with the lid ajar so the tank airs out, and keep the lithium pack charged but not left on a hot shelf.
products.bestFor: Lawn feeding on small to medium yards where a clean, steady band matters.

products.name: PetraTools HD2000-S Pro 2 Gallon Sprayer with 9 nozzles

specList.label: Pistol
specList.value: Heavy duty steel with adjustable patterns

products.description:
Nine nozzles are the headline, and for fertilizer that matters because the right tip is half the job. A wide flat fan lays liquid feed evenly over turf, a fine mist suits foliar feeding on shrubs, and a coarse tip handles drenching. The pro series adds a heavy duty steel spray pistol with adjustable patterns and a PetraJet style nozzle, so the part your hand works the most is metal instead of thin plastic.

The four foot hose and padded shoulder strap keep the tank on your hip and the wand in your hand, and the listing quotes about two hours of runtime from a rechargeable battery. That is shorter than the Scotts on quoted hours but plenty for a single feeding session. Because it has more parts, the Petra has more places to rinse after fertilizer, and the pistol and nozzle bodies need attention after each use.

Expect to clear salts from the pistol screen and to keep the spare nozzles in a labelled bag, because the tips look alike and you will want the fan tip for lawns and the mist tip for foliage. It sits at the upper end of the cost range here, which is fair for the metal pistol and the nozzle set.

products.name: BUDSTR 2 Gallon Battery Powered Sprayer, 8 gaskets
products.description:
Fertilizer is gritty stuff to mix, and a wide mouth tank makes it far easier to scoop in a measure, stir and see that everything has dissolved before the lid goes on. This unit has exactly that opening, plus a thickened tank wall and a 50 inch hose that resists kinking. The pump is a plain electric one, with no agitator or special chemical hardware claimed.

What sets it apart is the gasket pack: one fitted and seven spares. Fertilizer salts creep into thread seats and make lids weep, so a drawerful of seals is practical rather than gimmicky. It does not document Viton like the Scotts, so keep it to fertilizer, soap and mild sprays rather than concentrated herbicide.

Rinse the filter head on the pickup hose after every feed, because that is where undissolved granules lodge. Against the Lovydro it has the larger opening and more spares, and against the Scotts it lacks the lock on shut off but costs noticeably less.
products.bestFor: Budget minded lawn and bed feeding with a unit you can maintain yourself.
pros: Wide mouth makes measuring and stirring easy

products.name: SideKing 2 Gallon Battery Powered Sprayer, telescopic wand
products.description:
Three pressure levels let you match the output to the nozzle: a low setting for a fine mist on seedlings, a higher one for lawn drenching. The 2000mAh battery has an indicator, and the telescopic wand reaches into beds or up into shrubs. Pressure control is more helpful for fertilizer than raw power, because too much pressure makes fine drift that wastes feed.

The pump is a small electric unit, so treat it as a feeding sprayer and not a herbicide tool. Against the Budstr it adds pressure choice and a longer wand but gives up spare gaskets, and against the Scotts it has the telescopic reach but not the documented filter and seals.

Flush the pump with clear water after each feed, because dissolved fertilizer dries into a crust that jams a small diaphragm. Collapse the wand when carrying so the joint does not catch, and charge the battery after each use.
products.bestFor: People who want to dial in pressure for different plants.

products.name: Lovydro 2 Gallon Battery Sprayer, 3 speeds, 4 mist nozzles
products.description:
The Lovydro's small design choice that matters for fertilizer is the filter head on the four foot pickup hose: impurities are strained out before they ever reach the pump. That is the right place for a screen, because it protects the pump itself and not just the nozzle. Three speeds are shown on a display, and four mist nozzles give a fine droplet suited to foliar feeding.

The mist nozzles are the weakness for lawn feeding, where you generally want a flat fan that puts a controlled band on the grass. For shrubs, vegetables and container plants it is a better match. Against the SideKing it has the pickup filter and a visible speed display, but a narrower nozzle selection for turf.

Rinse the filter head after each feed and shake the tank before you start, since this unit does not agitate. Dry the outside of the handle before recharging, and store the hose coiled loosely.

products.name: EARTHCRAFT 5.3 Gallon Backpack Sprayer for DeWalt 20V
products.description:
For an acre of turf, the real constraint is how often you refill, and a 5.3 gallon backpack tank changes that. This one is built around DeWalt 20V batteries, which are not included, so it only makes sense if you already own a pack. A one touch automatic mixing system keeps the tank stirred, which solves the settling problem that liquid fertilizer causes on long jobs.

Pressure is adjustable from 45 to 90 PSI, a sensible window for broadcast feeding where you want a coarse band. Double padded shoulder straps carry the roughly forty pounds of liquid. Against the Scotts it covers far more ground per fill but costs far more once you factor in the battery, and it takes more effort to rinse because of the larger tank and mixing parts.

Flush the mixing circuit after each feeding, because a stirring system that sits with dried fertilizer in it will stick. Fill the tank only as much as you need so your back does not carry a full load for a half tank job.
products.bestFor: Large lawns where mixing and capacity matter and a DeWalt battery is already on hand.
pros: 5.3 gallons cuts refills on large lawns
Automatic mixing keeps feed blended
45 to 90 PSI window suits broadcast feeding
Double padded shoulder straps

buyingCriteria.explanation: Liquid fertilizer carries fine particles and salts that jam small diaphragm pumps. The Lovydro 2 Gallon puts a filter head on the pickup hose and the Scotts uses an in line filter at the shut off. A sprayer with no accessible filter is one you will clean with a pin, which damages the nozzle.

Many fertilizers settle in minutes, so the first part of the tank is weaker than the last. The EARTHCRAFT 5.3 Gallon has an automatic mixing system, but the 2 gallon units do not. If your sprayer cannot stir, shake the tank before every pass and mix smaller batches.

A flat fan lays liquid evenly across grass, while a mist tip suits foliar feeding. The Petra HD2000-S Pro ships nine nozzles, and the Lovydro offers four mist tips. Match the pattern to the plant, and avoid a narrow jet that will burn a stripe into turf.

Fertilizer labels give an application rate per area, so measure your lawn and know how many gallons you will spray. A 2 gallon sprayer such as the Budstr needs several fills for a typical lawn, while the EARTHCRAFT 5.3 Gallon may do it in two. Over application burns turf, so calibrate once with plain water.

The EARTHCRAFT needs a DeWalt 20V pack that is not included, while the Petra and Scotts units ship with their own batteries. Count the real cost: a sprayer plus a pack you do not own is a much bigger purchase than the sticker suggests.

Fertilizer salts are the enemy of small pumps. Units with wide mouths, like the Budstr, make rinsing easier, and spare gaskets help when lids weep. Always flush with clear water until it runs clean, and store with the lid ajar.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration and clogging
howWeEvaluated.description: Fertilizer salts and sediment are the main failure source, so we scored each sprayer on where its filter sits and how easy it is to clean. The Scotts and Lovydro led, and the SideKing relied on a smaller screen.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mixing and consistency
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which units can keep the tank agitated. The EARTHCRAFT is the only one with a mixing system, so the 2 gallon units were scored on how easy it is to shake and re-mix.

howWeEvaluated.title: Nozzles and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: The nine nozzles on the Petra HD2000-S Pro set the standard for pattern choice, while the Lovydro with four mist tips scored lower for turf.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and battery
howWeEvaluated.description: Tank size and battery arrangement were compared. The EARTHCRAFT needs a DeWalt 20V pack, so its real cost and fit were noted rather than assumed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, lid leaks and clogged screens are the usual complaints. We favored wide mouths and spare gaskets, like the Budstr eight gasket kit.

maintenance.task: Flush until the water runs clear
maintenance.why: Fertilizer salts crystallize in the pump and nozzle. Clear water before storage keeps them from forming a crust.

maintenance.task: Clean pickup and in line filters
maintenance.why: Undissolved granules lodge in filters. A rinse takes seconds and stops weak spray.
Fertilizer creeps into thread seats. A fresh gasket stops a slow leak down the side of the tank.
Lithium cells last longer when topped up and not left empty. Store partly charged in a cool place.

maintenance.task: Store dry with the lid ajar
maintenance.why: A closed damp tank grows mildew and smells. Open storage lets the poly dry fully.

faq.q: Can I use a battery sprayer for liquid fertilizer?
faq.a: Yes, provided the fertilizer is fully dissolved and the sprayer has a filter. Rinse the pump with clear water afterward because salts crystallize and clog small pumps.

faq.q: Why does my sprayer stripe the lawn?
faq.a: Stripes usually come from uneven walking speed or a narrow nozzle pattern. Use a flat fan tip, keep the wand at a steady height and overlap passes slightly.

faq.q: Do I need agitation for fertilizer?
faq.a: It helps if the product settles. Fully soluble liquids stay mixed for a tank, but suspensions benefit from stirring. The EARTHCRAFT has a mixing system, and others need a shake.

faq.q: How much fertilizer sprayer capacity do I need?
faq.a: Match tank size to your lawn and the label rate. A two gallon unit needs several fills for a typical lawn, while a 5.3 gallon backpack may need only a couple.

faq.q: Can the same sprayer be used for weed killer?
faq.a: It is safer to keep separate sprayers. Residue in the pump or hose can damage plants later. If you must reuse one, the Scotts with Viton seals is the better choice.

faq.q: How do I prevent over application?
faq.a: Calibrate with plain water first by spraying a marked area and measuring how much you used. Then match that rate to the fertilizer label.
